Agora Web SDK.header: Agora Web SDK, statistics of remote video and audio tracks and of the call on the receiving side, polled periodically

0.name: RecvBitrate
0.quote: The total bitrate (bps) of the received audio and video, represented by an instantaneous value.
0.reason: All audio and video bitrate received by this end; the original text says it is an instantaneous value and does not state how long the statistical window is, so different window lengths are acceptable under the definition. The single-track RemoteVideoTrackStats.receiveBitrate counts video only and is less close than this field.

1.name: receivePackets
1.unit: Packets, audio track original text says "total packets"
1.quote: The total packets of the received audio.
1.reason: For the per-track cumulative received packet count, subtracting two readings gives the received packet count within the window, covering only this one track. The description of the video track field with the same name is written as "The total bytes of the received video.", which does not match the field name; it looks like a documentation typo, and here the original text of the audio track is taken as authoritative.

2.name: RecvBytes
2.unit: bytes, original text "total number of bytes"
2.quote: The total number of bytes received, represented by an aggregate value.
2.reason: Total bytes received over the entire call; the source states it is a cumulative value, so subtracting two readings gives the bytes within the window.

3.name: transportDelay
3.context: RemoteVideoTrackStats (AgoraRTCClient.getRemoteVideoStats); RemoteAudioTrackStats has the same field
3.quote: The delay (ms) between a remote client sending the video and the local client receiving the video.
3.reason: This is the one-way delay from when the sender sends it to when this end receives it; the original text does not say whether it is the average within a window or a single measurement. The queuing delay also requires subtracting the minimum delay so far, so the historical minimum must be tracked manually.

4.name: transportDelay
4.context: RemoteVideoTrackStats (AgoraRTCClient.getRemoteVideoStats); RemoteAudioTrackStats has the same field
4.quote: The delay (ms) between a remote client sending the video and the local client receiving the video.
4.reason: One-way transmission delay, the quantity is correct, but it must be averaged over the window and then have the fixed 200 ms baseline subtracted; subtracting a constant is not a unit conversion, so it is labelled a different definition.

5.name: transportDelay
5.context: RemoteVideoTrackStats (AgoraRTCClient.getRemoteVideoStats); RemoteAudioTrackStats has the same field
5.quote: The delay (ms) between a remote client sending the video and the local client receiving the video.
5.reason: The SDK does not provide a minimum delay; the minimum of successive transportDelay readings must be tracked manually.

6.name: transportDelay
6.context: RemoteVideoTrackStats (AgoraRTCClient.getRemoteVideoStats); RemoteAudioTrackStats has the same field
6.quote: The delay (ms) between a remote client sending the video and the local client receiving the video.
6.reason: Each reading gives only one delay value; the in-window minimum must be approximated from multiple readings within the window, and a per-packet minimum cannot be obtained. Whether it can be labelled a different definition is disputed; it is labelled a different definition by measure.

7.name: transportDelay
7.context: RemoteVideoTrackStats (AgoraRTCClient.getRemoteVideoStats); RemoteAudioTrackStats has the same field
7.quote: The delay (ms) between a remote client sending the video and the local client receiving the video.
7.reason: Same as feature 6, both the window mean and the window minimum must be approximated from multiple readings, disputed, judged same quantity.

8.name: receivePackets
8.quote: The total packets of the received audio.
8.reason: There is no inter-arrival field. The window length divided by the number of packets received within the window approximates the average inter-arrival time, which is an averaging operation.

9.name: downlinkNetworkQuality
9.quote: It is calculated based on the downlink transmission bitrate, downlink packet loss rate, RTT (round-trip time) and jitter.
9.reason: There is no jitter field in the receiver statistics. The description of this downlink quality level mentions jitter, which is easily mistaken for jitter, but it only gives a composite level from 0 to 6 and no jitter value can be extracted, so it does not count.

10.name: currentPacketLossRate
10.unit: the original text does not state the unit or value range
10.quote: The packet loss rate of the received video in 400ms.
10.reason: The video packet loss rate within a 400 ms window at the receiver is by definition the packet loss rate within the window. But the original text does not state whether the value is 0 to 1 or a percentage; on the same page freezeRate is written as [0.0,1.0], this field is not, so the conversion factor cannot be determined, and per the dispute it is judged same quantity. It only covers a single track.

11.name: receivePacketsLost
11.quote: The total number of lost video packets that should be received.
11.reason: Only the cumulative number of lost packets, no count of loss events, so the average number of packets lost per loss event cannot be computed. Similar name, listed for reference.

12.name: receivePackets
12.quote: The total bytes of the received video.
12.reason: The video packet proportion is obtained only by dividing the difference in received packet count of the video track by the sum of the differences in received packet counts of the video track and the audio track; it is a multi-field combination. The quotation is the original description of the video track receivePackets, written as bytes, see the note for feature 1.

13.name: receivePackets
13.quote: The total packets of the received audio.
13.reason: The difference in received packet count of the audio track divided by the sum of the differences in received packet counts of the audio and video tracks; a multi-field combination.

14.name: not found
14.reason: The remote track statistics, call statistics, and network quality interfaces contain no probing packet related fields.

0.name: bytesReceived
0.unit: bytes, original text "Number of bytes received"
0.reason: The track statistics do not contain the received bitrate; it must be computed as the byte difference between two readings divided by the timestamp difference and then multiplied by 8, which is a rate computation. NetworkQualityBandwidthStats.actual says "the actual bandwidth used, in bits per second", but it belongs to a network quality event, and the documentation does not say where or over what window it is computed, so it is not selected. Regarding the cumulative judgment, the documentation does not state it; based on the SDK source code lib/stats/receiverreport.js, the bitrate and received packet count are computed from the difference between two readings.

1.reason: The per-track received packet count is a cumulative count; subtracting two readings gives the received packet count within the window, covering only a single track. Regarding the judgment of cumulativeness, the documentation does not say; based on the SDK source code lib/stats/receiverreport.js, the bitrate and received packet count are computed using the difference of two readings.

2.name: bytesReceived

Regarding the judgment of cumulativeness, the documentation does not say; based on the SDK source code lib/stats/receiverreport.js, the bitrate and received packet count are computed using the difference of two readings.

3.name: roundTripTime
3.reason: There is no delay field in the receive track statistics, only the round-trip delay of the locally published track, which is in the send direction and computed from peer feedback. Queueing delay also requires tracking the historical minimum and subtracting.

4.name: roundTripTime
4.reason: round trip rather than one way, and it belongs to the local send direction track, and subtract the 200 ms fixed baseline, labelled a different definition.

5.name: roundTripTime
5.reason: There is no minimum delay field; the minimum must be tracked by oneself from the round-trip time readings, and the definition is also round-trip.

6.name: roundTripTime

7.name: roundTripTime
7.reason: Same feature 6; disputed; labelled a different definition.

8.name: packetsReceived
8.reason: There is no inter-arrival field; the window length divided by the number of packets received within the window approximates the average inter-arrival time, which is averaging. As for the cumulative judgment, the documentation does not say; based on the SDK source lib/stats/receiverreport.js, the bitrate and packet count are computed from the difference of two readings.

9.name: jitter
9.reason: The documentation gives only the unit, not the algorithm. The SDK source getstats.js computes it by multiplying the browser statistic jitter by 1000 and truncating, not the standard deviation of within-window arrival intervals, labelled a different definition.

10.name: packetsLost
10.unit: Packets, original text "The number of packets lost"
10.reason: There is no ready-made packet loss rate; it requires the packet loss count difference divided by the sum of the packet loss count difference and the received packet count difference, which is a multi-field combination. NetworkQualityFractionLostStats.fractionLost only writes "packets lost", and neither the value range nor the calculation location is written, so it is not selected. For the cumulative judgment, the documentation does not say; based on the SDK source code lib/stats/receiverreport.js, the bitrate and received packet count are computed using the difference of two readings.

11.name: packetsLost
11.reason: Only the cumulative number of lost packets, no count of loss events, so the average number of packets lost per event cannot be computed. Similar name, listed for reference. Regarding the cumulative judgment, the document does not say; based on the SDK source code lib/stats/receiverreport.js, the bitrate and received packet count are computed from the difference of two readings.

12.name: packetsReceived
12.reason: The report splits the video track and audio track into two lists; the difference in received packet count for the video track divided by the sum of the received packet count differences for all tracks gives the video packet proportion, a multi-field combination. Regarding the cumulative judgment, the documentation does not say; based on the SDK source code lib/stats/receiverreport.js, bitrate and received packet count are computed from the difference between two readings.

13.name: packetsReceived
13.reason: The difference in received packet count of the audio track divided by the sum of the differences in received packet counts of all tracks; a multi-field combination. For the cumulative judgment, the documentation does not say; based on the SDK source file lib/stats/receiverreport.js, bitrate and received packet count are computed from the difference of two readings.

14.name: not found
14.reason: Neither the track statistics nor the network quality statistics contain any probing packet related fields.

9.reason: Exponentially smoothed with a 1/16 gain per RFC 3550 on the transmission time difference, it is a smoothed estimate, and the quantity is also not the standard deviation of arrival intervals; the unit also varies with the encoding clock, labelled a different definition.

10.name: fractionLost
10.context: Producer.getStats() entry with type "inbound-rtp" (one per RTP stream received)
10.unit: 8-bit fixed point, full scale 256, based on source lostInterval << 8
10.reason: When mediasoup acts as the receiver and generates RTCP reception reports, it computes the packet loss ratio from the difference between the expected number of packets and the actually received number of packets in this interval, stores it as an 8-bit fixed-point value, and dividing by 256 gives the in-window packet loss rate; the window length is the interval between two reception reports. 12.name: packetCount

13.name: packetCount

13.quote: The producer's statistics contain an entry for each RTP stream being received.
13.reason: Same feature 12; sum over streams with kind equal to audio and then divide; multi-field combination.

14.reason: These are the probing bytes that mediasoup itself sends out, belonging to the sender-side measurement, counted by bytes rather than by packets, and must also be combined with the total to compute a ratio; there is no probing count in the receive direction, and rtxBytesReceived mixes retransmissions and probing together. 12.reason: Sum the received packet count differences for streams whose Kind is video, then divide by the sum of the received packet count differences for all inbound streams, a multi-field combination.

13.name: PacketsReceived

1.name: packets

2.name: bytes
2.reason: The cumulative number of bytes received for each inbound media stream; subtracting two readings gives the number of bytes within the window. The judgment about cumulativeness is based on the source code ice.c, bytes += buflen.

3.unit: ms, based on the source code comment "We need milliseconds"
3.reason: The round-trip delay computed from the LSR and DLSR reported by RTCP, not one-way; queueing delay also requires tracking the minimum and subtracting.

4.name: rtt

4.reason: round trip rather than one way, and subtract the 200 ms fixed baseline, labelled a different definition.

7.name: rtt

7.reason: Same feature 6; disputed; labelled a different definition.

8.name: packets

13.name: packets

Regarding the cumulative judgment, the basis is the server source code rtpstats_receiver.go.

3.unit: the original text does not state it, the proto has no comment, and the server source code also does not state the unit

7.reason: Same feature 6; disputed; labelled a different definition.

8.reason: Average packet rate over the entire segment; only its reciprocal gives the average arrival interval, and it excludes pure padding packets, labelled a different definition. For interval judgments, the entire segment.

9.unit: microseconds, based on the server source jitter / clockRate * 1e6

10.reason: Cumulative packet loss percentage over the entire segment, not a within-window value, and differencing ratios does not give the within-window ratio either; the difference between packets_lost and packets must be recombined, labelled a different definition. For interval judgments, the entire segment.

12.name: packets
12.context: RTPStats per track, with TrackInfo.type (AUDIO / VIDEO)

13.name: packets
13.context: RTPStats per track, with TrackInfo.type (AUDIO / VIDEO)
13.reason: Same feature 12; sum over tracks with type equal to AUDIO and then divide.

14.name: packets_padding
14.reason: The server source code records packets with a payload of 0 as padding packets; probing commonly uses such packets, but padding packets are not necessarily all probing, and they must also be combined with the total received packet count into a ratio; this is disputed, so it is labelled a different definition.

6.name: msRTT

7.name: msRTT
7.quote: Smoothed round-trip time (SRTT), an exponentially-weighted moving average (EWMA) of an endpoint's RTT samples, in milliseconds.

9.name: not found

10.reason: Only gives the number of missing packets within the interval, must be combined with pktRecv to compute the ratio, and the original text says missing includes packets that have not arrived out of order, the definition is wide, judged same quantity.

13.name: not found

ns-3 FlowMonitor.header: ns-3 network simulator, FlowMonitor per-flow statistics (FlowStats) collected at the IP level and read during or after a simulation run

0.name: rxBytes
0.context: FlowMonitor::FlowStats (per flow, also serialized to XML)
0.quote: Total number of received bytes for the flow
0.reason: There is no received rate field; it requires the difference of two readings divided by the time difference and multiplied by 8, which is computing a rate.

1.name: rxPackets
1.context: FlowMonitor::FlowStats (per flow, also serialized to XML)
1.quote: Total number of received packets for the flow
1.reason: Cumulative number of packets received per stream at the receiving end node; subtracting two readings gives the received packet count within the window.

2.name: rxBytes
2.context: FlowMonitor::FlowStats (per flow, also serialized to XML)
2.unit: bytes, the original text says the probe counts the IP header
2.quote: rxBytes, rxPackets: total number of received bytes / packets for the flow;
2.reason: Cumulative received byte count per stream; subtracting two readings gives the byte count within the window.

3.name: delaySum
3.context: FlowMonitor::FlowStats (per flow, also serialized to XML)
3.unit: ns-3 Time object, XML output in nanoseconds, based on the source code As(Time::NS)
3.quote: delaySum: the sum of all end-to-end delays for all received packets of the flow;
3.reason: The in-window mean delay is obtained by dividing the delaySum difference by the rxPackets difference, and only after subtracting minDelay is it the queuing delay; a combination of three fields. The delay is the true one-way delay under the simulation global clock.

4.name: delaySum
4.context: FlowMonitor::FlowStats (per flow, also serialized to XML)
4.unit: ns-3 Time object, XML output in nanoseconds, based on the source code As(Time::NS)
4.quote: delaySum: the sum of all end-to-end delays for all received packets of the flow;
4.reason: Sum of one-way delays; to average within a window it must be combined with rxPackets, and the fixed 200 ms baseline must also be subtracted.

5.name: minDelay
5.context: FlowMonitor::FlowStats (per flow, also serialized to XML)
5.unit: ns-3 Time object, XML output in nanoseconds, based on the source code As(Time::NS)
5.quote: Contains the smallest measured delay of a received packet
5.reason: The smallest one-way delay among packets received since self-monitoring began is the minimum delay so far, read directly without subtraction. Multiply the nanosecond value output by XML by 1e-6 to get milliseconds; if the Time millisecond interface is called directly in C++, the coefficient is 1.

6.name: delayHistogram
6.context: FlowMonitor::FlowStats (per flow, also serialized to XML)
6.unit: seconds, histogram default bucket width 0.001 s
6.quote: delayHistogram, jitterHistogram, packetSizeHistogram: histogram versions for the delay, jitter, and packet sizes, respectively;
6.reason: Subtracting the delay histograms of two readings gives the delay distribution within the window; the lowest non-empty bucket approximates the minimum within the window, which is then divided by the average within the window obtained from the delaySum difference divided by the rxPackets difference, a multi-field combination limited by the bucket width.

7.name: delayHistogram
7.context: FlowMonitor::FlowStats (per flow, also serialized to XML)
7.unit: seconds, histogram default bucket width 0.001 s
7.quote: delayHistogram, jitterHistogram, packetSizeHistogram: histogram versions for the delay, jitter, and packet sizes, respectively;
7.reason: Same feature 6; within-window mean minus within-window minimum; requires combining the histogram difference and the delaySum difference; labelled a different definition.

8.name: timeLastRxPacket
8.context: FlowMonitor::FlowStats (per flow, also serialized to XML)
8.unit: ns-3 Time object, XML output in nanoseconds, based on the source code As(Time::NS)
8.quote: timeLastRxPacket: when the last packet in the flow was received;
8.reason: The difference between the timeLastRxPacket of two readings divided by the difference in rxPackets gives the average arrival interval within the window, a multi-field combination.

9.name: jitterSum
9.context: FlowMonitor::FlowStats (per flow, also serialized to XML)
9.unit: ns-3 Time object, XML output in nanoseconds, based on the source code As(Time::NS)
9.quote: jitterSum: the sum of all end-to-end delay jitter (delay variation) values for all received packets of the flow, as defined in RFC 3393;
9.reason: What is accumulated is the absolute value of the difference in one-way delay between two adjacent packets, that is, the delay variation of RFC 3393, not the standard deviation of inter-arrival times; judged same quantity.

10.name: lostPackets
10.context: FlowMonitor::FlowStats (per flow, also serialized to XML)
10.quote: lostPackets: total number of packets that are assumed to be lost (not reported over 10 seconds);
10.reason: The cumulative packet loss count must be combined with rxPackets to compute a ratio, and loss is only judged when nothing is seen for more than 10 seconds; losses within the window are counted with a lag; judged same quantity.

11.name: lostPackets
11.context: FlowMonitor::FlowStats (per flow, also serialized to XML)
11.quote: lostPackets: total number of packets that are assumed to be lost (not reported over 10 seconds);
11.reason: Only the total number of lost packets, no count of loss events, so the average number of packets lost per event cannot be computed. Similar name, listed for reference.

12.name: not found
12.reason: FlowMonitor classifies flows by 5-tuple and has no concept of media type.

13.name: not found
13.reason: FlowMonitor classifies flows by 5-tuple and has no concept of media type.

14.name: not found
14.reason: There are no probing packet related fields.
